author: Oscar
text:
Your glasses cost $5 to make. You paid $300. And one company you've never heard of is the reason why.

topReplies.text:
He said the first thing most people don't realize is that EssilorLuxottica isn't a big company. It's the entire industry — pretending to be hundreds of separate companies.

He said the third thing most people don't understand is the insurance trap — because the company that makes your glasses also owns the insurance company that tells you where to buy them.

He said the fourth thing most people don't know is that your "luxury" designer glasses were made on the same production line as every other pair — and the designer never touched them.

He said the fifth thing most people don't know is that lenses — the part that actually corrects your vision — cost almost nothing to produce.

He said the sixth thing most people don't know is that independent optometrists are often trapped inside the same system — and many of them know it.

topReplies.author: Oscar
topReplies.text:
He said the seventh thing — and the part where the thread shifts from problem to solution — is that alternatives exist. Real alternatives. And they cost 70–90% less.

He said the glasses monopoly feels inescapable because EssilorLuxottica controls the traditional retail channel.

topReplies.author: Oscar
topReplies.text:
He said the eighth thing most people get wrong is thinking online glasses can't be as good as optometrist-dispensed glasses. He said they're functionally identical — if you know your prescription and your measurements.

The most common objection to buying glasses online is: "But I need to try them on" and "My prescription is complicated." He said both concerns are solvable — and the industry amplifies them to protect its margins.

He said the ninth thing most people never consider is that the lens upgrades your optometrist pushes are the highest-margin upsells in the entire transaction — and most of them are available online for 80% less.

topReplies.text: I wear progressive (bifocal) lenses.  When I get them they have to see the frame on my face and they make a dot where the "line" should be so when I look straight ahead it is not the reading part.  How does that work on these online retailers you mention?

topReplies.text: We’ve been using EyeBuyDiect for years both single vision and progressive bifocals and never been disappointed. If I didn’t like the glasses, they refunded my money no problem.

topReplies.author: g00semagoo
topReplies.text: Tip: take a picture of the ruler in front of your eyes. Then read the measurement from the image. It's a lot easier than trying to read the measurement in a mirror.
